charters.name: claims_analyst
charters.description: Owns the cost and integrity of claims settlement: what is paid, how fast, and how much of it should not have been paid at all.
accountabilities: Reduce payments that should not have been made at the amount they were made
Reduce average settled claim cost without harming legitimate claimants
Reduce the time taken to settle a claim
charters.yaml:
# The acceptance test for the whole platform.
#
#   "If I give you claims data and an underwriting analyst role, can the system figure out
#    by itself what it should analyse?"
#
# This charter shares NO vocabulary with portfolio_analyst.yaml — different domain,
# different metrics, different actions, different burden of proof. If running both
# requires touching any code in loop/, the engine has a leak and the missing abstraction
# has just identified itself.
role: claims_analyst
version: 1
description: >
  Owns the cost and integrity of claims settlement: what is paid, how fast, and how much
  of it should not have been paid at all.

accountabilities:
  - id: reduce_leakage
    statement: Reduce payments that should not have been made at the amount they were made
    metric: leakage_flag
    direction: decrease
    horizon_days: 180
    priority: 1

  - id: control_severity
    statement: Reduce average settled claim cost without harming legitimate claimants
    metric: settled_amount
    direction: decrease
    horizon_days: 365
    priority: 2

  - id: speed_settlement
    statement: Reduce the time taken to settle a claim
    metric: days_to_settle
    direction: decrease
    horizon_days: 90
    priority: 3

decision_rights:
  - action_type: route_to_investigation
    description: Send a defined group of claims to the special investigations queue.
    autonomy_level: L2_act_reversible
    reversible: true
    blast_radius:
      unit: claims
      max_per_run: 200
    observation_metric: leakage_flag
    observation_lag_days: 60

  - action_type: fast_track_settlement
    description: Approve straight-through settlement for a defined low-risk group.
    autonomy_level: L1_recommend
    reversible: true
    blast_radius:
      unit: claims
      max_per_run: 1000
    observation_metric: days_to_settle
    observation_lag_days: 30

  - action_type: revise_reserve_guidance
    description: Change the reserving guidance applied to a class of claims.
    autonomy_level: L1_recommend
    reversible: false
    blast_radius:
      unit: claims
      max_per_run: 50
    requires_authority: chief_actuary
    observation_metric: settled_amount
    observation_lag_days: 365

# A stricter default than the portfolio role: acting wrongly on a claim harms a specific
# identifiable person, so the standing burden of proof is higher.
evidence_standards:
  min_sample_size: 150
  max_p_value: 0.01
  min_effect_size: 1.25
  multiple_testing_correction: benjamini_hochberg

evidence_overrides:
  revise_reserve_guidance:
    min_sample_size: 500
    max_p_value: 0.005
    min_effect_size: 1.3
    multiple_testing_correction: benjamini_hochberg
    requires_causal_design: true

constraints:
  leakage_features:
    - leakage_flag
  forbidden_features:
    # Routing on the assessor rather than the claim would optimise the measurement, not
    # the outcome.
    - assessor_name
  block_sensitive_columns: true
charters.markdown:
---
role: claims_analyst
version: 1
---
# Claims analyst
Owns the cost and integrity of claims settlement: what is paid, how fast, and how much of it should not have been paid at all.

## Accountabilities
### reduce_leakage — Reduce payments that should not have been made at the amount they were made
- metric: `leakage_flag`
- direction: decrease
- horizon: 180 days
- priority: 1

### control_severity — Reduce average settled claim cost without harming legitimate claimants
- metric: `settled_amount`
- direction: decrease
- horizon: 365 days
- priority: 2

### speed_settlement — Reduce the time taken to settle a claim
- metric: `days_to_settle`
- direction: decrease
- horizon: 90 days
- priority: 3

## Decision rights
### route_to_investigation — Send a defined group of claims to the special investigations queue.
- autonomy: L2_act_reversible
- reversible: yes
- cap: 200 claims per run
- observe: `leakage_flag` after 60 days

### fast_track_settlement — Approve straight-through settlement for a defined low-risk group.
- autonomy: L1_recommend
- reversible: yes
- cap: 1000 claims per run
- observe: `days_to_settle` after 30 days

### revise_reserve_guidance — Change the reserving guidance applied to a class of claims.
- autonomy: L1_recommend
- reversible: no
- cap: 50 claims per run
- observe: `settled_amount` after 365 days
- approval: chief_actuary

## Evidence standard
- min sample: 150
- max p: 0.01
- min effect: 1.25
- correction: benjamini_hochberg
- requires causal design: no
- requires holdout: no
- requires confound control: yes
### Override: revise_reserve_guidance
- min sample: 500
- max p: 0.005
- min effect: 1.3
- correction: benjamini_hochberg
- requires causal design: yes
- requires holdout: no
- requires confound control: yes

## Constraints
- never use: `assessor_name`
- leaks the outcome: `leakage_flag`
- sensitive columns: blocked

charters.name: hr_analyst
charters.description: Owns workforce retention and engagement. Finds where people leave and where satisfaction is low, and proposes reversible, manager-led interventions. A human reviews outcomes, not steps.
accountabilities: Reduce the share of employees who leave the organisation
Raise job satisfaction across the workforce
charters.yaml:
# A workforce role over a plain HR extract (data/hr_attrition.csv, the IBM attrition set with
# Attrition derived to a 0/1 column). Same code as the insurance roles: nothing here is
# special-cased. Protected attributes are forbidden explicitly as well as by the standing screens.
role: hr_analyst
version: 1
description: >
  Owns workforce retention and engagement. Finds where people leave and where satisfaction is
  low, and proposes reversible, manager-led interventions. A human reviews outcomes, not steps.

accountabilities:
  - id: reduce_attrition
    statement: Reduce the share of employees who leave the organisation
    metric: attrition_flag
    direction: decrease
    horizon_days: 365
    priority: 1

  - id: raise_satisfaction
    statement: Raise job satisfaction across the workforce
    metric: JobSatisfaction
    direction: increase
    horizon_days: 180
    priority: 2

decision_rights:
  - action_type: flag_for_stay_interview
    description: Add employees in a defined group to their manager's stay-interview list.
    autonomy_level: L2_act_reversible
    reversible: true
    blast_radius:
      unit: employees
      max_per_run: 100
    observation_metric: attrition_flag
    observation_lag_days: 180

  - action_type: recommend_policy_change
    description: Propose a change to a working-pattern or compensation policy for a defined group.
    autonomy_level: L1_recommend
    reversible: true
    blast_radius:
      unit: employees
      max_per_run: 500
    requires_authority: hr_director
    observation_metric: attrition_flag
    observation_lag_days: 365

evidence_standards:
  min_sample_size: 50
  max_p_value: 0.05
  min_effect_size: 1.2
  multiple_testing_correction: benjamini_hochberg

constraints:
  leakage_features:
    - attrition_flag
  forbidden_features:
    - Age
    - Gender
    - MaritalStatus
  block_sensitive_columns: true
  notes: >
    Protected attributes are listed here as well as caught by the standing screens, because in
    an HR setting the charter should say so in its own words.
charters.markdown:
---
role: hr_analyst
version: 1
---
# Hr analyst
Owns workforce retention and engagement. Finds where people leave and where satisfaction is low, and proposes reversible, manager-led interventions. A human reviews outcomes, not steps.

## Accountabilities
### reduce_attrition — Reduce the share of employees who leave the organisation
- metric: `attrition_flag`
- direction: decrease
- horizon: 365 days
- priority: 1

### raise_satisfaction — Raise job satisfaction across the workforce
- metric: `JobSatisfaction`
- direction: increase
- horizon: 180 days
- priority: 2

## Decision rights
### flag_for_stay_interview — Add employees in a defined group to their manager's stay-interview list.
- autonomy: L2_act_reversible
- reversible: yes
- cap: 100 employees per run
- observe: `attrition_flag` after 180 days

### recommend_policy_change — Propose a change to a working-pattern or compensation policy for a defined group.
- autonomy: L1_recommend
- reversible: yes
- cap: 500 employees per run
- observe: `attrition_flag` after 365 days
- approval: hr_director

## Evidence standard
- min sample: 50
- max p: 0.05
- min effect: 1.2
- correction: benjamini_hochberg
- requires causal design: no
- requires holdout: no
- requires confound control: yes

## Constraints
- never use: `Age`, `Gender`, `MaritalStatus`
- leaks the outcome: `attrition_flag`
- sensitive columns: blocked
- notes: Protected attributes are listed here as well as caught by the standing screens, because in an HR setting the charter should say so in its own words.

charters.name: portfolio_analyst
charters.description: Owns the value of an existing customer portfolio: how much of it stays, and how much of it deepens. Operates autonomously; a human reviews outcomes, not steps.
accountabilities: Increase the share of customers who hold more than one product
Reduce the share of customers who lapse
charters.yaml:
# A retention/growth role. Note what is NOT here: no questions, no workflow, no screens,
# no mention of cohorts or campaigns. Those are derived.
role: portfolio_analyst
version: 1
description: >
  Owns the value of an existing customer portfolio: how much of it stays, and how much of
  it deepens. Operates autonomously; a human reviews outcomes, not steps.

accountabilities:
  - id: grow_repeat_purchase
    statement: Increase the share of customers who hold more than one product
    metric: repeat_purchase          # must be a column of the dataset
    direction: increase
    horizon_days: 180
    priority: 1

  - id: protect_retention
    statement: Reduce the share of customers who lapse
    metric: lapsed
    direction: decrease
    horizon_days: 365
    priority: 2

decision_rights:
  - action_type: flag_for_outreach
    description: Add customers to a prioritised contact list for a human or an agent to work.
    autonomy_level: L2_act_reversible
    reversible: true
    blast_radius:
      unit: customers
      max_per_run: 500
    observation_metric: repeat_purchase
    observation_lag_days: 90

  - action_type: recommend_product_bundle
    description: Propose a product combination to offer a defined group.
    autonomy_level: L1_recommend
    reversible: true
    blast_radius:
      unit: customers
      max_per_run: 2000
    observation_metric: repeat_purchase
    observation_lag_days: 180

  # Deliberately granted but heavily constrained — this is what an evidence override is
  # for, and it demonstrates that not all actions clear the same bar.
  - action_type: change_pricing_factor
    description: Alter a pricing input for a defined group.
    autonomy_level: L1_recommend
    reversible: false
    blast_radius:
      unit: policies
      max_per_run: 100
    requires_authority: pricing_committee
    observation_metric: repeat_purchase
    observation_lag_days: 365

evidence_standards:
  min_sample_size: 100
  max_p_value: 0.05
  min_effect_size: 1.2
  multiple_testing_correction: benjamini_hochberg

evidence_overrides:
  change_pricing_factor:
    min_sample_size: 1000
    max_p_value: 0.01
    min_effect_size: 1.3
    multiple_testing_correction: benjamini_hochberg
    requires_causal_design: true    # observational gates can never satisfy this

constraints:
  # Columns that would leak the outcome into its own predictor.
  leakage_features:
    - repeat_purchase
    - lapsed
  block_sensitive_columns: true
  notes: >
    Identifiers and protected attributes are blocked by the platform's standing screens
    and do not need to be listed here.
charters.markdown:
---
role: portfolio_analyst
version: 1
---

## Accountabilities

- priority: 1

### protect_retention — Reduce the share of customers who lapse

### recommend_product_bundle — Propose a product combination to offer a defined group.

- autonomy: L1_recommend

charters.name: web_analyst
charters.description: Owns the health of a digital platform: which devices, sources and journeys throw errors, and where active use is falling. Proposes fixes for engineering to schedule; never ships code.
accountabilities: Reduce the share of events that hit a JavaScript error
Increase the share of events from active users
charters.yaml:
# A digital analytics role over a flattened GA4 event export (data/web_events.csv). The raw
# export carries device/geo/traffic as JSON blobs; the preset has them flattened to columns,
# because a gate can only test a bare column. Small data: the sample-size bar is set to match.
role: web_analyst
version: 1
description: >
  Owns the health of a digital platform: which devices, sources and journeys throw errors, and
  where active use is falling. Proposes fixes for engineering to schedule; never ships code.

accountabilities:
  - id: cut_js_errors
    statement: Reduce the share of events that hit a JavaScript error
    metric: is_js_error
    direction: decrease
    horizon_days: 30
    priority: 1

  - id: keep_users_active
    statement: Increase the share of events from active users
    metric: is_active_user
    direction: increase
    horizon_days: 90
    priority: 2

decision_rights:
  - action_type: raise_engineering_ticket
    description: Open a prioritised defect for a defined device, OS or traffic segment.
    autonomy_level: L2_act_reversible
    reversible: true
    blast_radius:
      unit: tickets
      max_per_run: 10
    observation_metric: is_js_error
    observation_lag_days: 14

  - action_type: recommend_traffic_change
    description: Propose pausing or reweighting a traffic source or medium.
    autonomy_level: L1_recommend
    reversible: true
    blast_radius:
      unit: sources
      max_per_run: 3
    requires_authority: marketing_lead
    observation_metric: is_active_user
    observation_lag_days: 30

evidence_standards:
  min_sample_size: 30
  max_p_value: 0.05
  min_effect_size: 1.2
  multiple_testing_correction: benjamini_hochberg

constraints:
  leakage_features:
    - is_js_error
    - is_active_user
  block_sensitive_columns: true
charters.markdown:
---
role: web_analyst
version: 1
---
# Web analyst
Owns the health of a digital platform: which devices, sources and journeys throw errors, and where active use is falling. Proposes fixes for engineering to schedule; never ships code.

## Accountabilities
### cut_js_errors — Reduce the share of events that hit a JavaScript error
- metric: `is_js_error`
- direction: decrease
- horizon: 30 days
- priority: 1

### keep_users_active — Increase the share of events from active users
- metric: `is_active_user`
- direction: increase
- horizon: 90 days
- priority: 2

## Decision rights
### raise_engineering_ticket — Open a prioritised defect for a defined device, OS or traffic segment.
- autonomy: L2_act_reversible
- reversible: yes
- cap: 10 tickets per run
- observe: `is_js_error` after 14 days

### recommend_traffic_change — Propose pausing or reweighting a traffic source or medium.
- autonomy: L1_recommend
- reversible: yes
- cap: 3 sources per run
- observe: `is_active_user` after 30 days
- approval: marketing_lead

## Evidence standard
- min sample: 30
- max p: 0.05
- min effect: 1.2
- correction: benjamini_hochberg
- requires causal design: no
- requires holdout: no
- requires confound control: yes

## Constraints
- leaks the outcome: `is_js_error`, `is_active_user`
- sensitive columns: blocked

Accountability.description:
An outcome the role owns, expressed as a measurable quantity and a direction.

The `metric` must be a column of the dataset the role runs against. This is what
forces charters to be honest: "improve customer relationships" cannot be written here,
because there is no measure to point at.
Accountability.title: Accountability

AutonomyLevel.description:
How much rope a role has for a given action type.

A role is not "autonomous" or "not autonomous" — autonomy is granted per action
class and earned by evidence in the outcome ledger. New action types start at
L1_RECOMMEND and are promoted only after their outcome record justifies it.
AutonomyLevel.title: AutonomyLevel

BlastRadius.description: The maximum damage a single action type can do in one run.
BlastRadius.title: BlastRadius

Constraints.description: What the role may not touch, regardless of what it discovers.
Constraints.title: Constraints

DecisionRight.description:
One thing this role is permitted to do, and how much rope it has.

Actions the charter does not name simply cannot be taken. There is no escape hatch —
an agent that invents an action type gets a hard refusal from `authorise_action`.
DecisionRight.title: DecisionRight

EvidenceStandard.description:
What counts as proof. Different actions warrant different burdens of proof.

Flagging a customer for a phone call and changing a pricing factor are not the same
decision, and should not clear the same bar.
EvidenceStandard.title: EvidenceStandard
